parsed.explanation: The objection is valid. Since Q is defined as the primes dividing A, P(x)\sigma(x) may contain primes at most A that do not divide A; A=15 and x=18 gives the stated example. Thus the induction’s disjointness contradiction fails, and its lemma is actually false under this definition. The later numerical discussion notices the needed finite set—primes at most A—but does not prove the lemma with that corrected definition. Replacing the definition of Q by all primes at most A, together with correcting the accompanying false sentence, repairs the proof locally.
